newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN TURN TO FIGHTING TALK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN TURN TO FIGHTING TALK.

text.p: Fighting talk is coming from AC Milan in their push to put a disastrous start to the season behind them.
The reigning champions, seventh in serie A and seven points adrift of leaders Juventus, travel to bottom club Reggiana on Sunday where anything less than victory would spell bitter disappointment.
Out of the European Cup and the Italian cup, and with old coach Arrigo Sacchi back after quitting the national team, they have only the league to look to in their bid to revive their glory days.
"From now on, every game we play will be like a final for us," said striker Marco Simone.
"Juve are certainly the strongest side at the moment but we can catch them and overtake them."
Sacchi stopped Milan's run of eight league and cup matches without a win last Sunday when his side beat Udinese 2-1.
He is expected to opt for experience at Reggiana, putting veteran Pietro Vierchowod alongside captain Franco Baresi in central defence.
The pair have more than 900 league matches between them, with Baresi up for his 450th game in serie A.
"We shouldn't be chasing Juve but trying to improve our position game by game and looking to overtake the clubs that are in front of us by just a few points," said Baresi.

Milan's Roberto Baggio is doubtful with sciatica and defender Alessandro Costacurta is suspended but Croat Zvonimir Boban should return from injury and Simone is expected to partner Liberian striker George Weah up front.
Reggiana are the only club without a win this season and have beaten Milan only once in six previous league ties.
So far this season they have reaped just five points.
Second-placed Vicenza, the surprise of the season, host Parma and need to win to stay in touch with the league leaders.

That could signal the end for Parma's embattled coach Carlo Ancelotti, whose team are entering serious danger in the lower reaches of the league and whose job is reportedly at risk in his first season at the club.
European and World Club champions Juventus went clear at the top of serie A in midweek when they demolished Udinese 4-1 and they are at home to second from bottom Verona.
But any thought that Juventus could forget the threat from AC Milan was abruptly dismissed on Friday by Alessandro del Piero, who scored twice from the penalty spot at Udinese.
"Call it an obsession, call it tradition but I'm convinced that Milan will be back among the contenders for the championship," he said.
"They've already paid for their mistakes at the start of the season. The worst is over for them."
